statement.p: The moment of inertia of a solid body about an axis in 3-space relates the angular acceleration about this axis to torque (force twisting the body). The moments of inertia about the coordinate axes of a body of constant density and mass m occupying a region W of volume V are defined to be I_x = \frac{m}{V}\int_W (y^2+z^2) \,dV\qquad I_y = \frac{m}{V}\int_W (x^2+z^2) \,dV\qquad I_z = \frac{m}{V}\int_W (x^2+y^2) \,dV
Use these definitions to find the moment of inertia about the z-axis of the rectangular solid of mass 24 given by 0 \le x \le 3, 0 \le y \le 4, 0 \le z \le 1.

static.solution:
V of the solid is 3 \cdot 4 \cdot 1 = 12. Thus for I_x we have I_x = \frac{24}{12}\int_W\, y^2 + z^2\,dV = 2\int_0^3\int_0^4\int_0^1\,y^2 + z^2\,dz\,dy\,dx. This is I_x = 2\int_0^3\int_0^4 y^2 z + \frac13 z^3\bigg|_{z=0}^{z=1} = 2\int_0^{3}\int_0^{4}\, 1 y^2 + \frac{1}{3}\, dy\,dx, or I_x = 2\int_0^3 \frac{64}{3} + \frac{4}{3}\, dx = 136.
Similarly, I_y = 80,\qquad\mbox{and}\qquad I_z = 200.
